title: Mukund Urges Mumbai Indians to Sign Indian Wicketkeeper, Release De Kock
excerpt: Speaking on JioStar, Abhinav Mukund said an Indian wicketkeeper was MI's missing piece and that he would release Quinton de Kock to free an overseas slot.
body:
• Former India cricketer Abhinav Mukund, speaking on JioStar, said Mumbai Indians' missing piece was an Indian wicketkeeper — he named no specific incoming player.
  • Mukund said relying on Ryan Rickelton or Quinton de Kock in the top seven pushed Tilak Varma down and blocked playing Sherfane Rutherford and Will Jacks together.
  • He would release de Kock — bought for ₹1 crore at the IPL 2026 auction and used in three games — solely to free an overseas slot.
  • IANS reports a November 17 retention deadline, with the IPL 2027 mini-auction set for December 16.

Former India cricketer Abhinav Mukund has urged Mumbai Indians to bring in an Indian wicketkeeper-batter before the IPL 2027 auction and to release South Africa's Quinton de Kock to free an overseas slot. Mukund named no specific Indian keeper as a target; his named recommendation was about who should leave.

"If you're talking about Mumbai Indians, the only thing, according to me, that was missing was an Indian wicketkeeper in there."

— Abhinav Mukund, on JioStar

Why the overseas keeper hurt the balance

Speaking on JioStar's 'Game Plan', Mukund said the lack of an Indian keeper was a big miss because, in their top seven, MI had to play either Ryan Rickelton or de Kock. That, he said, pushes Tilak Varma down the order and does not give the option to play both Sherfane Rutherford and Will Jacks, making it a confusing fit within the quota of four overseas players. According to ANI's reporting of his comments, Rickelton scored 448 runs in 12 innings in IPL 2026 at an average of 40.72 and a strike rate of 186.66, including a century and two fifties.

The squad as it stands

IANS reports that MI have not had an experienced Indian wicketkeeper since Ishan Kishan was released ahead of the IPL 2025 mega auction. Their current options are two foreign keepers, de Kock and Rickelton, plus the largely untested uncapped Robin Minz. De Kock, IANS and ANI both report, was bought at his base price of ₹1 crore at the IPL 2026 auction and played only three games, with Rickelton the first-choice keeper-batter; ANI credits de Kock with 132 runs in those three matches, including a century.

The Hardik trade context

Mukund's comments came as MI are reportedly set to trade Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings in exchange for Arshdeep Singh, according to IANS. Mukund said that if Hardik does go, it should be a win-win for all parties, and that what comes back in the trade affects whether MI need the extra overseas space he would create by releasing de Kock. IANS adds that Arshdeep would join a pace group already including Jasprit Bumrah, Deepak Chahar, Shardul Thakur and Trent Boult.

What happens next

The retention deadline is the immediate decision point — IANS reports it as November 17 — ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction on December 16, which ANI, citing Cricinfo, says will be held in Goa on the same day as the second India-Sri Lanka ODI in Bengaluru. Whether MI act on Mukund's advice will be visible first in their retention list.
